meta.title: Pantheus — Software designed around the way you operate
meta.description: Pantheus designs software around the way each business runs, easy for every role and updated every week. Pantheus Office for office teams, Pantheus Production for factories.

hero.title: Your business is <acc>one of a kind</acc>. Your software should be too.
hero.lead: Pantheus designs software around the way your business already runs, easy enough for everyone from managers to front-line staff. Every week brings an update, shaped by what your own users tell us.

office.desc: Tasks, projects, meetings, documents and chat, in one flow through the office day.

production.desc: ERP for the factory floor: bills of materials, planning, purchasing, inventory, production orders and finished goods.

problem.title: Big software makes you change how you work. Spreadsheets can't keep up.
problem.quote: “How many units can we build right now?”
problem.body: With spreadsheets, that question takes hours, and the answer is stale by the time it reaches you. Packaged software makes you bend your process to fit someone else's screens, and staff drift back to spreadsheets because it's hard to use. Pantheus builds the software from the way your work already flows.

approach.title: Built around how you work. Better every week. Easy for every role.

steps.d: Built around how you work today
steps.title: We start from how you work today.
steps.body: We follow the work as it really happens, from the moment materials arrive at the gate to the moment a document is posted to the ledger. For every event we ask the same six questions: who does it, when, with what data, how the status changes, which document records it, and what the exceptions are.
get: Software that fits the way you already work
What makes your business different is built in, not forced into a template
Your own names, forms and approval levels, exactly as you use them

steps.d: Feedback today, an update this week
steps.title: Hit a snag? Say so right there.
steps.body: Users press “Send feedback” on the screen they're using, with no call to make and no meeting to wait for. We ship small changes every week, so the software keeps up with how you work, even when the way you work changes.
get: A feedback button on every screen
Small, regular updates instead of one big release
Changing a process is no longer a six-month project

steps.title: Designed for the people doing the work, not only the ones reading reports.
steps.body: Managers usually choose the software, but storekeepers, accountants and office staff use it the most. We design each screen around the actions they repeat every day. When staff actually use it, the numbers managers see can be trusted.
get: Each role gets screens built around its own work
Step-by-step guides that run on the real screens
Short training, clean data from day one

principles.title: What you can count on with Pantheus.

items.label: Deploy your way
items.title: On your premises or in the cloud. Your choice.
items.body: Run the server inside your own network, or in the cloud if you'd rather not manage infrastructure. Either way, the data is yours.

items.label: Measured by outcomes
items.title: Every feature is tied to a number you care about.
items.body: Think inventory loss, line stoppages, or the days a purchase request sits waiting for approval. If a feature doesn't move a number, we don't build it.

items.label: On site
items.title: Our team works on site with yours.
items.body: We come to you to map the work, sit with your team through the first days on the new software, and walk each person through the real screens.

items.label: Built with AI
items.title: Ready to change when you do.
items.body: AI helps us write code faster, and our engineers stay responsible for the architecture and the tests. That keeps each change cheap, so we can say yes to more of them.

ai.title: Ask in plain language, get answers from your own data.
ai.body: The AI reads your operating data, such as documents, plans and tasks, so you don't have to dig through dashboards. Pan is live in Pantheus Office. Asking the factory questions in plain language is on the Production roadmap.
ai.placeholder: Ask about the factory, projects, stock…

We build for that one place first. You see the result in your real work before deciding what comes next.
Add workflows when the business needs them, in the order you choose. No big project to commit to up front.

closing.heading: Let's build software that fits how you work.
closing.lead: It starts with one conversation about how you operate today. There's no template to fit into and no lock-in.

meta.title: Pantheus Office — One workday, one flow
meta.description: Tasks, projects, meetings, documents, chat and purchase requests in one place, plus Pan, an AI assistant.

hero.title: One workday, one <acc>flow</acc>.
hero.lead: Tasks, projects, meetings, documents and chat in one place. Every screen is designed around the things people do many times a day.

stops.title: One office, one flow of work.
stops.desc: Click any area, or follow the route from switching on in the morning to settling purchase requests at the end of the day.

stops.title: Know what comes first the moment you log in.
stops.desc: The inbox gathers what needs you: overdue work, work due today and tomorrow, and unread notifications.

hots.b: Overdue work comes first, with its project and how many days late it is, so you don't have to dig through projects to find what you owe.
Drag a task onto your calendar as a block of time. Scheduling it doesn't change the task's start or due date.

stops.title: Minutes written right on the meeting page.
stops.desc: Who attended, how long it ran, what was decided: Office keeps all three on one page.

hots.b: Minutes are saved like any document, so a month later you can still find which meeting settled a decision.
Join the video call from the meeting page and attendance is recorded automatically. For in-person meetings, add an offline meeting and keep minutes the same way.

stops.title: Delivery projects run by phase and sign-off date.
stops.desc: Phases, steps and tasks on one Gantt chart. Sign-off dates sit on the timeline; a day late and the whole team sees it.
specs: Know which phase is slipping, and why

hots.b: Three levels on one Gantt chart, each phase collapsible. The sign-off date is its own milestone, flagged when late.

hots.t: A view for each kind of project
hots.b: Client projects run by phase, development teams use kanban, and day-to-day operations get a type of their own. Nobody has to force their work into one template.

stops.title: The description and the AI prompt in one task.
stops.desc: Coding work carries extra fields for developers and a Prompt block for a coding agent. The kanban has a Review column where a person checks what the AI did.
specs: Assign work to people and AI alike

hots.t: A prompt for the coding agent
hots.b: Write the request once, in a form people can read and an agent can run, instead of writing it twice.
The board has four columns: To do, Doing, Review and Done. AI work stops at Review until a person has checked it.

stops.title: Chat with the team, or ask Pan.
stops.desc: Groups and direct messages sit next to the work. Pan, the AI assistant, lives in the conversation list like a colleague.

hots.b: Ask about your work, projects and documents in Vietnamese or English. Pan can also draft a task from a message, and the task is only created once you confirm it.
Each department has its own group, such as accounting or the product team, so nothing gets buried in one big chat.

stops.title: The team's documents, tagged by topic.
stops.desc: The team's documents in one place, tagged by topic and browsable as a tree. Anyone can comment on a paragraph, with version history and export to Word or PDF when something has to go out.
specs: One home for what the team knows

hots.b: Arrange documents in a topic tree, such as internal, product or client, so even a new hire can find things on their own.
Files from tasks, chat and documents land in one library, with previews for images, PDFs and video.

stops.title: Request, approve, reimburse and settle, all without email.
stops.desc: Every request moves through clear stages: awaiting approval, awaiting purchase, awaiting transfer, awaiting settlement, recognized. A request can also be sent back for changes.

hots.b: Everyone can see which stage a request is at and who it's waiting on, so nobody has to ask “did I send it?”
Attach the VAT invoice and the proof of transfer right on the request; at least one is required before it can be marked as bought.

meta.title: Pantheus Production — ERP for small and mid-sized factories
meta.description: Bills of materials, planning, purchasing, inventory, production orders and finished goods on one flow of data. Rolling out at an electric vehicle factory.

hero.title: <acc>One flow of data</acc> from materials at the gate to finished goods in stock.
hero.lead: ERP for small and mid-sized factories in Vietnam: bills of materials, planning, purchasing, inventory, production orders and finished goods. It is rolling out at an electric vehicle factory, and new workflows are added every week.

facts.v: Rolling out at an EV factory
Your factory's server or the cloud

stops.title: One factory, one flow of data.
stops.desc: The dotted line is the material flow: from the truck at the gate, through the store and onto the line, until it leaves as a finished product. Each stop is one step in that flow, with its own document.
specs: At the factory or in the cloud

hots.b: The start-of-day screen: slips awaiting approval, today's orders short on materials, materials to buy. Each tile opens exactly the list to work through.

stops.title: Versioned bills of materials, per colour.
stops.desc: Set up materials, colours and the bill of materials (BOM) for each product. Sub-assemblies like the seat have their own BOM. Every change goes through a draft, so the active version is never overwritten.
specs: Material needs right for every colour

hots.b: Edit a draft, activate it when it's ready. Change history is kept; export to Excel any time.
Each colour of a product has its own materials list. A sub-assembly like the seat is a product with a BOM of its own.

stops.title: From weekly output to a list of materials to buy.
stops.desc: Enter the planned output for the week. The system multiplies out the BOM, subtracts stock and incoming deliveries, and shows what needs buying.
specs: A buy list, ready to order

hots.b: Press “Calculate shortfall” and the numbers are ready, without VLOOKUPs or waiting for someone to sign them off. Raise purchase orders straight from the result.
Before locking in the plan, see how many units current stock can build and which material is holding you back.

stops.title: Orders per supplier, receipts tied to the order.
stops.desc: Split the buy list into one order per supplier. When the truck arrives, the storekeeper creates a goods receipt against the order, and the order then shows how much has arrived and how much is still due.
specs: Every delivery matched to its order

hots.b: Receive in parts across several receipts; the order shows received against ordered.
Approving an order and receiving it are tracked as separate statuses. Receiving has three levels of its own: not received, receiving and fully received.

stops.title: Stock is a ledger, not a cell you type into.
stops.desc: Every stock figure is derived from approved receipts, issue slips and stock counts. When the numbers drift, you count, approve an adjustment, and the change is logged.
specs: Goods receipt · Issue slip · Stock count

hots.b: A slip goes from draft to awaiting approval to approved, and only approved slips change stock. If one is approved by mistake, a manager cancels it with a reason and the system posts a reversing entry.
Create a stock count, enter what was actually counted, approve to adjust stock. Quickly filter materials below minimum or negative.

stops.title: One production order, issue slips generated for you.
stops.desc: Operations creates the day's order; the system calculates materials from the BOM and generates the issue slips. The storekeeper just picks and approves.
specs: The right materials, in full, on time

hots.b: One “Generate issue slip” button fills in materials and quantities from each order line's BOM.
Each order line knows whether its issue slip is draft, awaiting approval or approved, and whether its finished goods have been received.

stops.title: Finished goods received from the production order.
stops.desc: Completed products go into stock on a finished goods receipt tied to the order. Finished stock by code and colour, traceable to every receipt.
specs: Know exactly how many vehicles are in stock

hots.b: Stock by code, colour and unit, calculated from approved documents.
Double-click a row to open its stock ledger: every receipt and issue that changed the stock of that code.

stops.title: Warranty looked up by VIN.
stops.desc: Customers or dealers check warranty by VIN; defects are logged by material and supplier. This part is still planned.

hots.b: A public page where entering the VIN shows the warranty end date, with no need to phone the call centre.
Group defects by material and supplier, as evidence for returns and supplier choice.

tour.title: Follow the material flow.
tour.body: Every physical step in the factory creates a document, and the software follows those steps exactly. Click a number to jump to an area, or + for details.
tour.screenNote: The screen below follows the stop you pick above. The data is illustrative; the name and logo are your factory's.

items.b: Step-by-step walkthroughs for each job, such as production orders and issue slips, planning and purchase orders, or stock counts. They run on the screen you're already using.
Admins can see the system exactly as someone in operations or a storekeeper sees it, so they can help without guessing.
There's a “Send feedback” button in the corner. Report a problem right where you got stuck, and see it fixed in the next update.

Every slip records who created it, who approved or rejected it, and when. If a slip is approved by mistake, a manager cancels it with a reason and the system posts a reversing entry, so nothing is overwritten.
A daily production order generates its issue slip, with materials and quantities taken from the bill of materials. The storekeeper just picks and approves, with no lines to retype.
The software carries your factory's name and logo. Pantheus appears only in one “Powered by” line.

deploy.title: On your factory's server or in the cloud. Your data stays in your hands.

items.t: At the factory or in the cloud
items.b: Run the server on the factory's local network, or in the cloud if you'd rather not manage infrastructure. Each legal entity gets its own database.
With the server at the factory, the warehouse and the line keep working even when the internet connection drops.
Automatic backups every day, with the last 30 days kept.
Export any list to Excel at any time, so your data never gets stuck inside the software.
If two people edit the same slip, whoever saves second gets a warning instead of silently overwriting the first.
Each update is built and tested before it reaches your server, so a new version every week costs you no installation work.

roadmap.title: An open roadmap, updated against a real factory.
roadmap.body: Our customers' bottlenecks decide what we build next.

items.b: Bring the system into daily operation at the first electric vehicle factory, together with the store and operations teams.
Print labels and scan them when finished goods are received; open a vehicle's production order from its VIN.
A public lookup page, warranty slips, and replacement parts deducted straight from stock.
Group defects by material and supplier, as evidence for returns and supplier reviews.
Stock movement by period, output by order, material consumption against the BOM.
Ask in plain language: what do we need to buy this week, which supplier causes the most defects.

closing.heading: Start with your factory's most expensive bottleneck.
closing.lead: One walk along the material flow with your team. Then we propose what to build first, and what can wait.
